note: Friday 2 Oct 2026, ~07:02am SGT run, BEFORE Asia's open and before tonight's US payrolls. Latest COMPLETED US cash session = Thu 1 Oct close, a calm, broadly positive-breadth session following Wednesday's thin-breadth fade: S&P +0.19% to 7,666.45, Nasdaq +0.04% to 26,871.60, Dow +0.04% to 50,926.56, Russell +0.35% to 2,806.63, VIX +0.31% to 16.39. The actual ISM Manufacturing PMI printed 54.5% (vs 54.8 forecast, 54.6 prior) -- a slight miss but still a 9th straight month of expansion -- while its Prices sub-index jumped to 77.9% from 71.1%, a genuine cost-push cross-current. Initial jobless claims beat forecast at 197K (vs 201K expected), the lowest since July. The week's biggest regime shift: Fed-funds odds for the Oct 27-28 FOMC flipped decisively toward a hold after the cooler core PCE (released Wed 9/30) and the soft ISM print -- Kalshi/Polymarket now price roughly 65-66% hold / 33-34% hike, reversing the ~65-69% hike odds priced just a day earlier -- and the 10Y eased to ~5.24% after touching its highest intraday level since 2002. Gold and silver rallied in a genuinely aligned ETF/futures move (GLD +0.50% to 382.76, GC=F +0.46% to 4,205.80; SLV +0.94% to 55.02, SI=F +2.05% to 61.33), even as miners (GDX -1.21%, NEM -0.58%, GOLD -1.13%) diverged lower -- a profit-taking signal in the equity-miner sleeve worth flagging. Oil staged a genuine rally this time (USO +2.99% to 150.02, CL=F +2.91% to 93.05, XLE +1.95% to 62.70) on reports the Trump administration has no intention of easing Iran sanctions, continued Iranian resistance to reopening the Strait of Hormuz, and an unexpected EIA inventory draw; Brent (BZ=F -1.01% to 102.48) lagged, a genuine regional-spread divergence. Credit remains a live, intensifying watch item: CCC-and-below OAS has widened further to above 1,000bps, its widest since 2023 (near the 100th percentile of post-2023 history), even as the broad HY index stays comparatively tight. China's Golden Week stimulus continues to meet a skeptical market (CSI 300 down ~6% in September, ~12% over three months) as investors wait for more direct consumption/property support. Rare-earth basket pulled back broadly after its recent run (MP -2.54% to $46.09, UUUU -2.90% to $10.71), and LYC.AX plunged -8.60% to A$12.64 on its own news -- Lynas announced a ~US$672M all-share acquisition of Meteoric Resources (ASX:MEI), a dilutive, execution-risk-driven sell-off, not a China-truce development. Separately, the China-US rare-earth export-control suspension was confirmed extended to 10 Jan 2027 (not 10 Nov 2026 as previously tracked), per the Trump-Xi summit -- CSIS reads the shorter-than-hoped extension as signaling US dissatisfaction with China's offers, so it remains a live, not resolved, re-escalation risk, just pushed further out than this file previously tracked. BTC held firm at $84,676.87 (+1.34%). Tonight's main event: September Non-Farm Payrolls, Average Hourly Earnings, and the Unemployment Rate, all due 2 Oct 20:30 SGT, with an unusually wide forecast dispersion (BofA 60K, Goldman 80K, Dow Jones consensus ~84-89K, Reuters survey ~100K, vs August's 162K; unemployment rate forecast 4.1% vs 4.1% prior) -- the dominant swing catalyst into the Oct 27-28 FOMC. Tokyo Core CPI y/y (forecast 2.4% vs 1.8% prior) is due 2 Oct 07:30 SGT, essentially concurrent with this run, so treat it as not-yet-confirmed.

Jobless claims beat forecast at 197K (vs 201K expected), the lowest since July, pointing to a still-resilient labor market hours ahead of tonight's payrolls (due 20:30 SGT; forecast dispersion is unusually wide -- BofA 60K, Goldman 80K, Dow Jones consensus ~84-89K, Reuters survey ~100K -- vs August's 162K). Separately, Lynas Rare Earths (LYC.AX) plunged -8.6% on its own news -- a ~US$672M all-share acquisition of Meteoric Resources announced same-day -- a dilution/execution-risk sell-off, not a China-truce development; the China rare-earth export-control suspension itself was confirmed extended to 10 Jan 2027 (not 10 Nov 2026), pushing out but not resolving the re-escalation risk.
